title: Active Leisure Tents Recalled Due to Fire Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Costco
summary: The tents do not meet the flammability label claim on the unit, posing a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 19,000.

title: Fashionviews Inc. Recalls P.Jamas Children's Sleepwear Due to Violation of Federal Flammability Standard
summary: The garments fail to meet federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear, posing a risk of burn injury to children. Units: About 4,000.

title: Stained Glass Soldering Irons Recalled By Cooper Tools Due to Burn Hazard
summary: The power cord can break at the flex point where the cord attaches to the handle, posing a burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 69,000.

title: Williams-Sonoma Recalls Hot Chocolate Pots Due To Burn and Laceration Hazards
summary: The handle of the hot chocolate pot can break off during use, posing burn and laceration hazards. Units: About 28,000 units in the United States and 700 in Canada.

title: Arms Reach Concepts Recalls Infant Bed-Side Sleepers Due to Entrapment Suffocation and Fall Hazards
summary: When the fabric liner is not used or is not securely attached, infants can fall from the raised mattress into the loose fabric at the bottom of the bed-side sleeper or can become entrapped between the edge of the mattress and the side of the sleeper, posing risks of suffocation. Units: About 76,000.

title: Pampers® Natural Stages Pacifiers Recalled by Key Baby Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The pacifiers fail to meet federal safety standards and pose a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 29,000.

title: Infantino Recalls Toy Activity Trucks Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The plastic beads on the activity truck's bead runs can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 40,500 in the United States and 1,900 in Canada.

title: Aquarium Heaters Recalled by United Pet Group Due to Fire and Laceration Hazards
summary: A wiring problem can cause the aquarium heaters to overheat or break during normal use, damaging the aquarium and posing fire and laceration hazards to consumers. Overheating can cause the heater to shatter or the aquarium glass to break. Units: About 1.2 million.

title: Children's Scooters Recalled by Kiddieland Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: A child's finger can get caught in the hinge mechanism between the steering column and the platform, posing a laceration hazard. Units: About 16,000 in the United States and 700 in Canada.

title: Disney Princess Plastic Trikes Recalled by Kiddieland Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The plastic castle display and the princess figures protruding from the top of the handle bar pose a laceration hazard if a child falls on it. Units: About 9,000 in the U.S. and 700 in Canada.

title: Photon Climbing Carabiners and Quickdraws Recalled Due to Risk of Injury
summary: The carabiner gate may open under a heavy load, posing a risk of serious injury or death if the climber falls. Units: About 15,500.

title: Pacific Trade International Recalls Candles Due to Fire and Burn Hazard
summary: The candles have a clear, plastic cup that can melt or ignite, posing a fire and burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 615,195 sets (about 7.48 million candles).

title: Lithium-Ion Batteries Used with Bicycle Lights Recalled by GeoManGear Due to Fire Hazard
summary: The lithium-ion batteries can overheat, posing a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 16,600 in the United States and 1,500 in Canada.

title: Spot Recalls Satellite Communicator Due To Loss of Emergency Communications Capability
summary: The internal voltage regulator can stop working, resulting in the inability to transmit messages and tracking information in emergency situations. Units: About 15,400.

title: ADP Recalls to Repair Unit Heaters Due to Fire Hazard1
summary: Some heaters were manufactured without a required flame rollout switch, which is a back-up device that shuts down the heater in the event of a heater failure. This poses a fire hazard. Units: About 400.

title: Lennox Industries Recalls to Repair Garage Heaters Due to Fire Hazard
summary: Some heaters were manufactured without a required flame rollout switch, which is a back-up device that shuts down the heater in the event of a heater failure. This poses a fire hazard. Units: About 440.

title: Wrist Rattles and Baby Booties Recalled by Midwest-CBK Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The pom-poms attached to the wrist rattles and booties can detach, posing a choking hazard. Units: More than 10,000 wrist rattles and 11,000 pairs of baby booties in the United States and 600 wrist rattles and 700 pairs of baby booties in Canada.

title: Cub Cadet Recalls Riding Lawn Mowers Due to Fire Hazard
summary: A fuel leak can occur near the rear mounting screws on the bottom of the fuel tank, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 4,300.

title: Girl's Clothing Recalled by My Michelle Due to Risk of Lead Exposure
summary: The jewelry and decorative trim attached to the girl's garments contain high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects. Units: About 90,000.

title: Redken 5th Avenue NYC Recalls Guts Spray Mousse Foam Due to Risk of Rupture
summary: The aerosol container's liner can corrode over time, posing a risk of the cans rupturing and expelling its contents. Units: About 1 million.

title: Rogue Fitness Barbell Brackets Recalled by Coulter Ventures Due to Injury Hazard
summary: The weld between the bracket and the pin that holds the barbell bracket in place on a weightlifting rack can break, causing the weights to fall, and posing an injury hazard to consumers. Units: About 5,500.

title: Cribs Recalled by ducduc Due to Fall and Entrapment Hazards
summary: The bottom rails on the crib sides can separate from the sides when the mattress is in the lowest position, causing the spindles to separate and the mattress to drop. This poses fall and entrapment hazards for young children. Units: About 330.

title: Heartland America Recalls Wooden Stools Due to Fall Hazard
summary: The legs and seat of the stool can crack and break, causing the consumer to fall. Units: About 5,850.

title: Toro Recalls Power Clear Snowblowers and Recycler Mowers Due to Fire or Burn Hazard
summary: The carburetors on both products develop fuel leaks and can ignite when exposed to an ignition source, posing a fire or burn hazard. Units: Snowblowers:  About 18,000 in the U.S. and 5,000 in Canada  Mowers:  About 6,000 in the U.S. and 200 in Canada.
